key_insight: CToM teaches an LLM to predict how a user will respond, then uses that prediction to self-revise before replying, improving collaborative multi-turn performance.
engineering_relevance: For interactive AI systems, this offers a practical way to reduce back-and-forth and improve task success by making the model anticipate user feedback during dialogue.
method: Draft an initial response to the user task.
Predict the user's likely reply to that draft and train with negative log-likelihood on the actual reply.
Combine response prediction with GRPO so the model optimizes both accuracy and interaction efficiency.
evidence_signal: Across mathematical reasoning, coding, and writing, CToM outperforms baselines; on a collaborative math task it raises final accuracy from 74.1% to 79.6% versus naive GRPO, while reducing user replies by 8% on coding and 17% on writing under matched reward.
watch_item: The approach adds an extra prediction objective and depends on high-quality interaction data, so gains may be sensitive to domain shift or user behavior that is hard to predict.
paper_title: Collaborative Theory of Mind: Learning to Self-Revise by Anticipating User Responses
